tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on The Battle of Marathon (490 BC)

questions.question: Q: Why did Darius invade Greece in 490 BC?
questions.correctAnswer: To punish Athens and Eretria for supporting the Ionian Revolt and to extend Persian control into mainland Greece. Darius also wanted to restore Hippias as a puppet tyrant in Athens.

questions.question: Q: How did Miltiades win the Battle of Marathon?
questions.correctAnswer: Miltiades strengthened both wings of the Greek line while thinning the centre. When the Greeks advanced, the strong wings crushed the Persian flanks, then turned inward to attack the Persian centre from both sides (double envelopment). The Persians fled to their ships.

questions.question: Q: Why was the decision to attack controversial?
questions.correctAnswer: The ten Athenian strategoi were split 5-5 on whether to attack or wait. The Persians had more troops and feared cavalry. Miltiades persuaded the polemarch Callimachus to break the tie in favour of attacking, arguing that waiting would allow more Persian allies to arrive.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on The Battle of Marathon (490 BC)

questions.question: Q: Why could Sparta not help at Marathon?
questions.correctAnswer: Sparta was celebrating the festival of Carneia, during which military activity was forbidden by religious law. Pheidippides reached Sparta the day after leaving Athens, but the Spartans said they could not march until the full moon. They arrived after the battle was over.

questions.question: Q: What was the significance of the Athenian victory at Marathon?
questions.correctAnswer: It proved that the Greek hoplite phalanx could defeat a larger Persian force, boosted Greek morale and confidence, and demonstrated that Persia was not invincible. It became a defining myth of Athenian identity and democratic superiority.
